feedback.0: Only changing the number of protons changes the element.

questions.explain: More electrons than protons → negative ion.

questions.text: Mass number = number of protons + number of ___. In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of ___.
questions.explain: Electrons are too light to count in the mass number; in a neutral atom, electrons = protons.

questions.prompt: Particle X has 8 protons, 8 neutrons and 10 electrons. What is it?
questions.explain: 8 protons = oxygen; 2 extra electrons = 2− charge: the oxide ion O²⁻.

questions.prompt: Explain why the mass of an atom is almost all in its nucleus.
questions.modelAnswer: The nucleus contains the protons and neutrons, which each have a relative mass of 1. Electrons have a tiny mass (about 1/1840 of a proton), so even though they take up most of the space, they add almost nothing to the mass.
rubric: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus and have mass 1
Electrons have a very tiny mass
So nearly all mass is in the nucleus
questions.explain: Nucleus = almost all the mass, tiny volume; electrons = almost all the volume, tiny mass.
